claims.text: Localized impetigo: a topical antistaphylococcal antibiotic for 5 to 7 days; mupirocin is the most used in the US, and topical treatment is as effective as or more effective than oral
claims.quote: The treatment for localized impetigo is a topical antistaphylococcal antibiotic for 5 to 7 days. Mupirocin is most commonly used in the United States. Alternatives include ozenoxacin, retapamulin, and fusidic acid; the latter two are not available in the United States. Topical treatment (eg, mupirocin, fusidic acid) is as effective or more effective than oral treatment for localized impetigo (2).

claims.text: Mupirocin 2% ointment is recommended for initial treatment of mild nonbullous and bullous impetigo (SORT A)
claims.quote: Topical antibiotic therapy with mupirocin 2% ointment is recommended for the initial treatment of mild, nonbullous and bullous impetigo.20,23,25,29 | | A

claims.text: Nasal mupirocin for S. aureus nasal carriers, a potential source of recurrent impetiginization.
claims.quote: Nasal mupirocin is recommended for patients who are nasal carriers of Staphylococcus aureus, a potential source of recurrent impetiginization.

claims.text: Decolonization significantly lowers S. aureus infection, but whether it lowers recurrent impetigo specifically is less clear
claims.quote: Decolonization in chronic staphylococcal nasal carriers may be effectively achieved by administering topical antibiotics (mupirocin), which causes a significant reduction in the rate of S. aureus infection (3); however, whether such decolonization lowers rates of recurrent impetigo specifically is less clear.
